findings.issue: Iteration 10 is explicitly recorded as the cap, but production code was changed and published in iteration 13 and the workflow has now run an eighteenth implementer tick. The current bookkeeping-only tick correctly makes no production change but cannot undo the cap violation.
findings.consequence: Another implementation tick in this workflow would violate the governing stop condition.
findings.correction: Stop this loop after this review, preserve the published linear history without reset/revert/force operations, and carry product findings into a separately authorized run.

findings.criterion: 7 and cross-cutting security — mandatory idempotency for Super Admin tenant creation
findings.issue: POST /v1/platform/tenants remains replaySafe rather than idempotent. definePlatformRoute therefore executes the handler when Idempotency-Key is absent, and the recorded route test succeeds without that header. Retrying a lost keyless request re-enters provisionTenant; with no requested slug its collision branch chooses a random suffix and creates another tenant.
findings.consequence: One intended Super Admin action can create duplicate properties, owners, inventory, policy, and audit history.
findings.correction: Require Idempotency-Key on tenant creation, update every caller/test to send a stable key, reject keyless requests, and prove exact-key replay returns one property. Cover a lost-response retry and in-flight double submission through the rendered Platform form.

findings.criterion: 7 and cross-cutting data integrity — atomic, recoverable platform creation/idempotency
findings.issue: The platform reservation insert, create_tenant call, tenant initialization transaction, business result, and replay finalization remain separate commits. There is no lease, reconciliation, compensation, or durable operation-to-tenant identity. A failure after tenant creation or business commit can leave an incomplete tenant and/or status=0 permanently; exact-key retry is then blocked while a fresh key can create a random-suffixed duplicate.
findings.consequence: A property can be stranded or partially initialized, and recovery can duplicate it.
findings.correction: Atomically bind creation/initialization and idempotency completion, or persist a unique operation identity that can reconstruct or safely complete the one property. Add fault-injection coverage after create_tenant and after business commit but before replay finalization.

findings.criterion: 6 and 7 — recoverable local-auth person and owner onboarding
findings.issue: Local onboarding persists only the generated password hash, while both replay stores replace temporaryPassword with null. A lost first response therefore replays 201 without the sole credential. People/Platform then report an invitation even though local auth created no invitation, and the forgot/reset UI is exposed only for external auth.
findings.consequence: A created member or a new property's only owner can be unable to sign in.
findings.correction: Add a recoverable setup/invitation or authenticated credential-reset flow with an explicit replay outcome while keeping secrets out of replay storage. Test lost-response retries for owner, tenant member, and platform member through successful first local sign-in.

findings.issue: Rendered tests execute Share branches and decode a guest QR, while API tests separately cover two-hour expiry, HMAC rejection, and stored verify_code mismatch; however, the joined test starts from a fabricated token, mounts GuestPass directly, replaces the scanner, and mocks lookup/redeem. No recorded execution joins server-generated bytes to the actual Share control, routed unauthenticated /pass bootstrap, decoded guest QR, and real gate validation.
findings.consequence: The exact artifact produced by the live resident flow has not been shown to survive sharing and redeem as the same valid pass.
findings.correction: In a future authorized run, execute a routed mobile-browser story from live issue through Share, /pass#t=…, QR decode, and real lookup/redeem. Assert exact token identity, two-hour unused expiry, HMAC tamper rejection, and stored verify_code mismatch rejection.

findings.criterion: 3 and 4 — real camera plate scanning at check-in and check-out
findings.issue: Rendered tests replace LiveCamera with a button that emits an already-decoded plate. No recorded run executes getUserMedia, the shipped ONNX loader/decoder, a camera fixture, and responsive browser rendering; the existing real-camera script covers check-in only.
findings.consequence: Actual camera acquisition and model decoding remain unverified in the shipped stack for both required flows.
findings.correction: In a future authorized run, record 390x844 real-model fake-camera check-in and checkout stories, including visible filled fields, checkout match/result, model/browser/fixture versions, stopped tracks, and a clean console.

findings.criterion: 6 and 7 — complete real-stack CRUD and cross-property operations
findings.issue: Rendered tests mock every API and complete a full lifecycle only for a unit; person is create-only, site/zone/slot lifecycle coverage is incomplete, cross-property coverage is one mocked member POST, and jsdom innerWidth does not exercise CSS layout. The available real-stack CRUD script is desktop-only and has no recorded run for this loop, person lifecycle, or Super Admin second-property operations.
findings.consequence: Persisted all-entity administration, complete cross-property Super Admin behavior, server authorization boundaries, and narrow-screen usability remain unverified in context.
findings.correction: In a future authorized run, execute full person/site/unit/slot lifecycles through the real routed UI/API at a narrow viewport, perform representative all-entity operations in a second property as Super Admin, and prove regular-admin server denial.
